clusters.proposedTitle: Share an event or a calendar: choose the right access
clusters.originalContribution: Original matrix: one-event guest, private editable calendar, read-only subscription, public URL. Show acceptance and ownership checks, and explain why family subscription access differs from shared calendar data.
clusters.publicationGate: Verify Cloud Calendars native sharing mechanism and recipient requirements; avoid assuming Apple or Google steps are its own.

clusters.proposedTitle: Choose a calendar view for the question you need answered
clusters.originalContribution: Compare spotting free time, reading full event titles, finding a date and reviewing a busy month using one original illustrative week. No best-app rankings.
clusters.publicationGate: Verify exact supported views and tablet layout.

clusters.proposedTitle: Choose a month, next-event or agenda widget
clusters.originalContribution: Explain purpose, visible-calendar selection and private event-title exposure. Diagnose an absent event by first checking app view and selected calendars. Use current Apple widget documentation before instructions.
clusters.publicationGate: Verify supported Cloud Calendars widget families/surfaces and refresh limits; never promise instant refresh.

clusters.proposedTitle: Keep work and personal plans readable in one calendar
clusters.originalContribution: Use a simple color/visibility scheme, clarify hiding is not deletion, and make a weekly availability review. Separate calendar filtering from permission changes.
clusters.publicationGate: Verify Cloud Calendars filtering and coloring controls; no claim of Focus Filter integration without proof.

clusters.proposedTitle: Find which layer is hiding a calendar event
clusters.originalContribution: Decision sequence: locate owning provider, verify event exists there, check account and calendar visibility, compare another device, then provider-specific support. Distinguish missing history from lost data.
clusters.publicationGate: Read full official troubleshooting bodies; do not copy destructive reset/full-sync advice or guarantee recoverability.
